evidence_statement: Merged new OT.02 consists of former Rietgors 762 ha, Fuut 367 ha and Kievit 373 ha; total 1502 ha.
intended_use: Historical design-area context and component stratification
guardrail: Do not use 1502 ha as current affected compaction area or assume it is the latest administrative area.

evidence_statement: Onderbemaling Tollebeek OT.02 is listed at 1497 ha.
intended_use: Administrative system-area benchmark and independent geometry cross-check
guardrail: Administrative area is not the same as affected area; current owner polygon is the admitted spatial identity.

evidence_statement: OT.02 target surface-water level is NAP -6.20 m.
intended_use: Managed boundary context
guardrail: Target level is not total dynamic pump head and is not an event initial groundwater condition.

evidence_statement: De IJsvogel has three large screw pumps with combined installed capacity of 540 m3/min.
intended_use: Installed-capacity benchmark for pump asset
guardrail: Installed capacity is not guaranteed incremental availability and is not total OT.02 effective capacity.

evidence_statement: Three Archimedes screws have a combined capacity of 9 m3/s.
intended_use: Independent corroboration of the 540 m3/min installed benchmark
guardrail: Secondary regional source; owner-backed source remains primary.

evidence_statement: De Kievit is described with two electrically driven vertical screw pumps of 30 m3/min each at 1.40 m head.
intended_use: Nominal physical asset benchmark
guardrail: Do not equate with verified post-2020 operational Q-H curve or with the 2009 calculated hydraulic capacity.

evidence_statement: The Kievit capacity was calculated in 2009 at 1.44 m3/s.
intended_use: Historical calculated-capacity context
guardrail: Keep separate from nominal hardware capacity and current operating capacity.

evidence_statement: The Kievit and IJsvogel underdrainage areas are coupled and form one peilgebied.
intended_use: Water-system topology
guardrail: Coupling does not imply unconstrained transfer or additive effective capacity.

evidence_statement: During extreme conditions IJsvogel can discharge part of the water from the Kievit area.
intended_use: Directional dispatch semantics
guardrail: No default assist fraction or conveyance capacity is supported by this source; reverse routing is not established.

evidence_statement: The under-pump installation was renovated in summer 2020; pump components, lubrication, check valves and switch cabinet were renewed and the electrical installation allows more efficient operation.
intended_use: Post-renovation asset-state context
guardrail: Do not infer a numerical post-renovation efficiency or capacity without acceptance tests or telemetry.

evidence_statement: Historical NOP SWAP/FutureView setup used 100 d as standard tile-drain resistance.
intended_use: Historical drainage sensitivity prior
guardrail: Not a calibrated current OT.02 parameter.

evidence_statement: Historical setup represented surface drainage with about 30 d resistance at groundwater 30 cm below surface and a drainage base 30 cm below surface.
intended_use: Historical wet-state drainage mechanism prior
guardrail: Mechanism prior only; do not silently transfer to current OT.02 implementation.

evidence_statement: PDOK IMWA exposes current peilgebied features suitable for discovery/corroboration of peilgebied geometry.
intended_use: Current harmonised geometry corroboration route
guardrail: Owner-hosted feature authority is primary for the admitted OT.02 polygon; PDOK remains a harmonised cross-check route.

evidence_statement: The owner-hosted ArcGIS directory exposes zzl_Peilgebieden and Peilbesluiten_WFL1; a separate legacy peilgebieden layer exposes GPG identity, area and level fields but reports Data Last Edit Date 2020-10-12.
intended_use: Owner-specific geometry acquisition and freshness reconciliation
guardrail: Use the newer owner services for feature authority; the 2020 legacy layer is not current geometry authority by itself.

evidence_statement: Owner layer zzl_Peilgebieden / Peilgebieden Besluit contains OBJECTID 232, GPGIDENT OT.02, GLOBALID c07f3d9b-c063-42c3-ba0a-1ff65a1b9c6a with status 4 (vigerend definitief), NAP -6.20 m summer/winter peil and an EPSG:28992 polygon whose Shape__Area is 14965219.5704 m2; the feature was last edited 2025-05-12 and is persisted canonically at data/spatial/tollebeek_ot02_current.geojson.
intended_use: Current peilgebied spatial identity and sampling-domain geometry
guardrail: This is not affected compaction area. Source attribute GPGOPPVL=1506 conflicts with geometry-derived ~1496.52 ha and is not admitted as exact geometry area; use the polygon itself.

evidence_statement: Owner Peilbesluiten_WFL1 Winterpeil and Zomerpeil surfaces contain OT.02 status-4 records with the same Shape__Area and Shape__Length and NAP -6.20 m as the admitted owner polygon; older OT.02 variants are status 11 and marked vervallen, while P-OT.02 is a separate status-1 practice record.
intended_use: Independent owner-surface status and geometry cross-check for current OT.02 identity
guardrail: Do not substitute status-11 obsolete variants or the status-1 P-OT.02 practice record for the admitted status-4 definitive geometry.

evidence_statement: Coordinate queries return derived/modal soil profile attributes including horizons, texture, bulk density and Staring building-block information.
intended_use: Soil-profile screening route
guardrail: Derived/modal profile is not a direct measurement and API bulk density is not automatically current compaction state.

evidence_statement: The review describes reduced gas transport/aeration and water infiltration under compaction and notes that the process most limiting to crop growth depends on soil and weather conditions; impeded root-system expansion due to mechanical resistance is identified as a major productivity mechanism.
intended_use: Support state- and context-dependent response theory
guardrail: Does not define a universal response magnitude for a given bulk density or compaction class.

evidence_statement: Long-term field experiments commonly compare experimentally compacted plots with plots receiving no additional experimental compaction; those controls can still be normally compacted and the measured penalty therefore represents additional experimental compaction rather than the gap to a never-compacted soil.
intended_use: Support contextual reference-state semantics
guardrail: Do not interpret a field-experiment control as a universal uncompacted reference.

evidence_statement: Compaction-related reductions in vertical infiltration, saturated hydraulic conductivity and subsoil water storage can promote perched water, ponding, lateral flow and surface runoff.
intended_use: Support the physical source-response pathway from soil state to runoff
guardrail: Mechanistic support does not provide a local runoff coefficient or event transfer factor.

evidence_statement: The paper identifies limited knowledge of compaction extent/severity at large scales and the difficulty of attributing off-site costs, and calls for linking profile-scale soil-function knowledge to catchment and regional hydrology.
intended_use: Support explicit scale-transfer layer
guardrail: Does not qualify a direct plot-to-catchment scaling factor.

evidence_statement: The economic analysis defines a baseline counterfactual as the soil condition that would prevail in the absence of degradation and sets that counterfactual in the context of each dominant managed soilscape.
intended_use: Support contextual counterfactual/reference-state concept
guardrail: The UK soilscape counterfactual is a conceptual precedent, not a Dutch soil-state parameterization.

evidence_statement: The framework distinguishes on-site costs, mainly private costs such as farm yield loss, from off-site costs that are mainly external costs borne by third parties; off-site valuation can require both market and non-market values.
intended_use: Support separation of private, public/external and societal valuation concepts
guardrail: Do not copy UK cost shares or unit values into current Dutch calculations.

evidence_statement: For national assessment the study classified 40 soilscapes from combinations of ten land-cover classes and four broad soil types, with state factors such as climate and topography modifying degradation likelihood.
intended_use: Support soil × land-use aggregation architecture as a precedent
guardrail: The specific UK classes and degradation probabilities are not transferable coefficients for the Netherlands.

evidence_statement: The national soilscape method explicitly did not intend local-scale assessment of degradation probability, intensity gradients or local associated costs.
intended_use: Support separation between national exposure aggregation and local process modelling
guardrail: Do not use high-level soilscape categories as a substitute for event/process modelling where local hydrology is required.

evidence_statement: The report states that thickness of the compacted layer and thickness of the layer above it strongly affect hydrological results and recommends thin discretisation in and around strongly contrasting compacted layers.
intended_use: Support explicit depth/layer geometry in SWAP source-response models
guardrail: Method guidance is not a numeric hydraulic parameterization for a new location.

evidence_statement: The report recommends hourly precipitation for accurate study of compacted-layer effects, especially for calculation of surface runoff.
intended_use: Support event/sub-daily forcing requirement for runoff qualification
guardrail: Does not establish that hourly forcing is sufficient for every short-duration event or catchment transfer problem.

evidence_statement: In one reported modelling comparison using 2008 hourly rainfall, annual surface runoff was 14 mm for compacted soil and 4 mm without compaction.
intended_use: Order-of-magnitude/context benchmark demonstrating potentially material hydrological response
guardrail: Case-specific model result; not a universal compaction-to-runoff coefficient and not directly transferable to Tollebeek.

evidence_statement: The report notes that modelled transpiration and groundwater responses depend on soil type, meteorological conditions and the chosen lower boundary; a closed lower boundary retains surplus water differently from free drainage.
intended_use: Support explicit boundary-condition provenance in current/reference comparisons
guardrail: Do not compare results from different boundary configurations as if the difference were caused only by compaction.

evidence_statement: The exploratory Dutch study estimated agricultural subsoil-compaction costs ranging from about EUR 80/ha/year for dairy farming on sandy soil to about EUR 300/ha/year for arable farming on light sandy clay and stated that the Dutch extent of the problem had not yet been quantified.
intended_use: Historical Dutch economic context and external benchmark
guardrail: Historical exploratory estimate; not a current unit cost and not a national damage coefficient.

evidence_statement: The report describes restricted rooting, infiltration and aeration under subsoil compaction and notes that reduced infiltration can increase surface runoff and nutrient transport to surface water.
intended_use: Support Dutch-context hydrological/external-effect pathway
guardrail: Qualitative synthesis; not a quantified event transfer relation.

evidence_statement: The study couples a soil-compaction-agroecosystem model with CMIP6 climate projections to simulate compaction-related changes in crop yield, nitrogen losses, soil carbon stocks and surface runoff across European arable land.
intended_use: Support multi-service/scenario architecture and comparison benchmark
guardrail: Continental future-climate modelling is not a current Netherlands calibration source.

evidence_statement: Simulations use winter wheat, three compaction levels represented by 4, 6 and 8 Mg wheel loads, five climate models and SSP585 future-climate horizons.
intended_use: Define transferability limits of Romero-Ruiz model outputs
guardrail: Do not apply reported European economic or runoff results directly to current Dutch soilscapes or other crops.

evidence_statement: Two deterministic 500 m grids, offset by 250 m in x and y, sampled 117 points strictly inside the admitted OT.02 polygon; 113 returned SoilPhys modal profiles, 4 returned no soil information, and eight distinct source-profile IDs were detected.
intended_use: Bounded OT.02 profile-context screening basis
guardrail: Grid fractions are diagnostic sampling fractions, not exact areal weights; SoilPhys profiles are derived/modal and are not direct local measurements or current compaction states.

evidence_statement: The official BOFEK2020 translation workbook maps all eight SoilPhys source-profile IDs detected in OT.02 to BOFEK2020 units 3001, 3004, 3005, 3015, 4004, 4006, 4018 and 4019.
intended_use: Profile-to-BOFEK2020 semantic crosswalk
guardrail: This crosswalk does not establish exact BOFEK polygon area inside OT.02 and does not convert modal profile density into current soil state.

evidence_statement: The Flevoland field campaign used 305 agricultural sampling locations. Fieldwork ran from September 2020 through June 2021. Dry bulk density was measured with three undisturbed 100 cm3 rings at a fixed 30 cm depth and a field-selected variable depth, with laboratory determination according to ISO 11272:2017. Penetration resistance was measured with a calibrated Eijkelkamp penetrologger using ten measurements per location.
spatial_scope: Agricultural Flevoland; exact OT.02 subset not yet resolved
intended_use: Qualified direct-measurement protocol and candidate point-data source for current-state acquisition
guardrail: Protocol quality does not identify which measurements fall inside OT.02 and does not make 2020-2021 measurements automatically representative of 2026 conditions.

evidence_statement: The study concludes that the measured data and available spatial covariates did not support a usable regional map of disturbing compacted layers in Flevoland.
intended_use: Prevent regional interpolation from being used as local OT.02 CURRENT-state evidence
guardrail: Do not infer OT.02 state values, affected area or profile weights from the unsuccessful regional map or province-wide summary percentages.

evidence_statement: The official Flevo - land in beweging project record states that more than 300 conventional point measurements were collected and that a valuable province-wide dataset was assembled.
intended_use: Acquisition route for source geocoordinates and measurement values needed to test for OT.02 observations
guardrail: Dataset existence does not establish public availability, an OT.02 subset or current 2026 representativeness. Raw coordinate/value records remain required.

evidence_statement: A reproducible intersection of the owner zzl_Drainage layer with the admitted OT.02 polygon found 74 drainage polygons. Their clipped union covers 1425.807934 ha, 95.27% of the 1496.521957 ha OT.02 polygon. The layer exposes spacing, installation-date and depth fields, but all 74 intersecting records return spacing 0 and null depth/date; layer data last edit is 2021-06-27.
intended_use: Owner parcel-drainage inventory and acquisition route for selected-unit drainage evidence
guardrail: Spacing 0 is treated as unavailable/sentinel-like here, not a physical zero spacing. The layer does not provide usable current drain depth, installation date or SWAP resistance.

evidence_statement: The owner Noordoostpolder water-system Legger service, data last edited 2025-08-27, intersects OT.02 with 127 Afvoervak lines (~55.57 km clipped length), 258 culvert features (~3.06 km clipped line length), 12 stuw points and 5 put points, plus other water-system structures.
intended_use: Current owner-backed open-water and water-system topology acquisition route
guardrail: Open-water topology is not subsurface tile-drain spacing/depth and does not determine SWAP drainage resistance. Publicly reviewed notice concerns the second design/draft legger, so final legal status of every feature is not independently asserted.

evidence_statement: Owner-hosted Noordoostpolder water-heritage documentation describes systematic subsurface parcel drainage installed mainly during 1946-1955, with drain spacing varying by soil and drainage discharging toward parcel ditches.
intended_use: Structural context for the importance of subsurface drainage in the Noordoostpolder
guardrail: Historical installation geometry is not a current OT.02 asset register and must not be promoted to present-day spacing, depth or resistance.

evidence_statement: Waterschap Zuiderzeeland identifies the 1998 Tollebeek water-overload event and reports 87.5 mm rainfall within 24 hours at the Marknesse measurement point.
intended_use: Owner-backed event identity and independent magnitude corroboration
guardrail: The narrative 87.5 mm value does not define the canonical hourly distribution or an exact UTC window; use the KNMI station series for numerical forcing.

evidence_statement: Owner historical documentation states that it had rained for days before the Tollebeek flood, the ground was fully saturated, and about 75 mm fell during the night of 27-28 October 1998.
intended_use: Antecedent-wetness chronology and event-window corroboration
guardrail: Narrative saturated-ground context is not an admitted initial soil-water or groundwater profile and the 75 mm figure is not used to synthesize hourly forcing.

evidence_statement: KNMI station 273 Marknesse provides 144 consecutive hourly records for the admitted forcing context 1998-10-24T00:00Z through 1998-10-30T00:00Z. The maximum rolling 24-hour rainfall in the acquired window is 88.4 mm from 1998-10-27T06:00Z through 1998-10-28T06:00Z. The canonical forcing file SHA-256 is 6c4ca1277523af73f26f6340ec8ebce5d52f42b6040085f7d50ecc78c5ca3c8a; selected wind, temperature, dewpoint, radiation, precipitation, visibility and relative-humidity fields are complete across the 144-hour context.
spatial_scope: KNMI station 273 Marknesse; Tollebeek event forcing proxy
intended_use: Observed station-based meteorological forcing baseline for the first Tollebeek paired source-model experiment
guardrail: Station forcing is not an exact spatial rainfall field over OT.02. Native units and trace semantics are preserved; SWAP-specific conversion/interpolation and hydrological initial state require separate qualification.

evidence_statement: Two historical GLD series inside the admitted OT.02 polygon are tied to GMW000000053815 (NITG B20F0038; RD 173300,522600; registered ground level NAP -4.58 m). Tube 1 screen is NAP -16.3 to -17.3 m and tube 2 is NAP -41.8 to -42.8 m. On 1998-10-14 the two source series report heads of NAP -4.93 m and -4.88 m, respectively; both historical observations are classified onbekend. The next observations are 1998-11-13 at NAP -4.85 m and -4.80 m.
spatial_scope: Inside admitted Tollebeek OT.02 polygon at GMW000000053815
intended_use: Historical deep piezometric-head anchor and initial-state acquisition-route evidence
guardrail: Deep-screen piezometric heads are not an observed phreatic groundwater table or depth-resolved root-zone initial state. Historical observation status is onbekend; do not infer a hydrostatic profile from these heads without separate hydrogeological and representativeness qualification.

evidence_statement: A systematic BRO screening of GLD series whose registered time span covers 1998-10-24 and whose monitoring-tube screen top lies 0-5 m below registered ground level found four shallow historical candidates within 10 km of OT.02 and zero inside the admitted OT.02 polygon. The closest is 1079.3 m outside with its nearest observation 6.392 days after the target date; all four selected shallow historical series use observation class/status onbekend.
spatial_scope: Admitted OT.02 plus 10 km historical groundwater discovery buffer
intended_use: Bounded negative evidence for the public shallow-groundwater observation route and definition of the remaining initial-state blocker
guardrail: Absence of a qualifying public shallow series inside OT.02 is not evidence of absence of historical shallow groundwater observations in owner or unindexed archives. Do not spatially interpolate outside shallow candidates into OT.02 as an admitted initial state.

evidence_statement: The nearest shallow-screen public candidate is GLD000000056353 / GMW000000053990 (NITG B20F0195), 1079.3 m outside OT.02, screen top 2.5 m below registered ground, with NAP -4.98 m on 1998-10-30. A temporally closer shallow candidate GLD000000060522 / GMW000000025540 is 3527.3 m outside, screen top 1.0 m below ground, with NAP -4.52 m on 1998-10-26. Both historical series are status onbekend.
spatial_scope: Near Tollebeek OT.02; outside admitted polygon
intended_use: Context for plausibility review and future archive targeting only
guardrail: These outside observations are not spatially representative enough to initialize OT.02 and are not admitted as a project groundwater-level input.

evidence_statement: The official 2006 Tollebeek peilbesluit retains the prior peil regime and documents separate underbemalingen OT02 De Rietgors, OT03 De Fuut and OT04 De Kievit, each with streefpeil NAP -6.20 m. The listed pump capacities are 2.600, 0.670 and 1.000 m3/s respectively, and all three pump directly to the Urkervaart. The same decision states that actual water levels fluctuate around target and may rise more than 0.20 m during heavy persistent rainfall.
intended_use: Historical system topology, target-level and nominal-capacity context for reconstructing the 1998 managed boundary
guardrail: This is near-period official system evidence, not a 1998 event water-level, pump-runtime or realized-discharge series. The 2006 capacities must not be treated as exact 1998 realized discharge without event evidence.

evidence_statement: Waterschap Zuiderzeeland states that after the 1998 Tollebeek water-overload event multiple stuwen were added, a new connecting watercourse was built in 2010, larger culverts and embankments followed in 2011-2012, and new gemaal IJsvogel opened in 2012. The owner describes the old Fuut and Rietgors pumps as 40 and 156 m3/min and IJsvogel as 540 m3/min.
time_scope: 1998 event context and post-1998 redesign through 2012
intended_use: Exclude the current merged/IJsvogel control system from silent use as the October 1998 managed boundary
guardrail: Post-1998 works and current IJsvogel capacity are not 1998 boundary inputs. The retrospective does not supply exact 1998 water-level or realized-discharge time series.

evidence_statement: Owner historical documentation describes the October 1998 crisis as occurring after days of rain and fully saturated soil, with about 75 mm overnight on 27-28 October; the Marknesser Sluis overflowed, a crisis centre was active and both large emergency pumps and about twenty smaller fire-brigade pumps were deployed while large flows moved toward low-lying Tollebeek.
intended_use: Event-control context showing that ordinary target-level/nameplate operation was insufficient and emergency intervention formed part of the actual 1998 boundary system
guardrail: The narrative does not provide exact pump locations, start/stop times, discharge hydrographs or water-level series and cannot be converted into a numerical boundary by assumption.

evidence_statement: Waterschap Zuiderzeeland provides a formal water-information request route for maps and measurement results that are not available through its public online information. This is the owner route for requesting historical 1998 water levels, pump logs/runtime/discharge records, stuw/inlaat operation and related archival boundary evidence.
time_scope: request route reviewed 2026-09-16 for 1998-10-24 through 1998-10-30 evidence
intended_use: Acquisition route for event-specific managed-boundary evidence
guardrail: A qualified request route is not the requested dataset. DR_SM_MANAGED_BOUNDARY remains partial until actual event evidence or a separately qualified reconstruction protocol is available.

evidence_statement: The official 2006 Tollebeek peilbesluit lists the dominant land use in historical De Rietgors (OT02) as arable agriculture with forest, De Fuut (OT03) as arable agriculture, and De Kievit (OT04) as arable agriculture with forest.
intended_use: Broad near-period land-use context for the 1998 source-model domain
guardrail: Near-period broad land use does not identify parcel-level crop identity, crop phenology or field condition in October 1998.

evidence_statement: LGN3 provides 25 m historical land-use/crop classes. For Flevoland the agricultural classification is based on 1995 satellite imagery, so it can provide spatial pre-event context for Tollebeek but not a direct 1998 observation.
intended_use: Pre-event land-use/crop context and candidate spatial screening route
guardrail: Do not copy a 1995 crop class into 1998; annual crop rotation can change crop identity without a stable land-use change.

evidence_statement: LGN4 is based on 1999/2000 satellite imagery and supports land-use change analysis relative to LGN3. It can provide post-event spatial context around Tollebeek but does not directly observe the 1998 growing season.
intended_use: Post-event land-use/crop context and broad stability review
guardrail: Do not backcast a 1999/2000 crop class to 1998 or interpolate crop identity between LGN3 and LGN4.

evidence_statement: LGN methodology explicitly notes that changes in agricultural crop type can reflect crop rotation rather than real land-use change, so crop classes are not a temporally continuous state that can be interpolated between map editions.
intended_use: Guardrail for temporal transfer of crop classes into the 1998 event
guardrail: Crop rotation prevents treating agreement/disagreement across historical map years as proof of the exact crop on an intermediate event date.

evidence_statement: PDOK documents annual public historical Gewaspercelen datasets for 2009 through 2022, with each annual dataset representing user-drawn agricultural parcels and declared crop around a 15 May reference date. No 1998 public annual BRP dataset is offered through this historical route.
intended_use: Bound the public annual parcel/crop acquisition route for the 1998 event
guardrail: Absence from this public PDOK archive is not proof that no 1998 crop records exist in institutional, owner, farmer or paper archives; it only means this route does not resolve the event.

evidence_statement: SWAP5 current Status-A documentation pins scientific production baseline 50346642bd565f79134ea17d5462e544b354998c with scientific production tree 3b085d7dea3d3f3fce42ad9d8f259a8350205846.
intended_use: Candidate pinned scientific executable authority for the first Tollebeek source-model pair
guardrail: This pin does not choose Tollebeek drainage, initial state, dynamic managed boundary, crop/vegetation or CURRENT/REFERENCE soil-state values.

evidence_statement: SWAP5 current Status-A documentation identifies 992a5c657bfe10a10100f92e0cb77c4825ae65b6 as the current Status-A acceptance authority and explicitly states that it is later than the scientific production baseline without introducing a scientific production postimage change.
intended_use: Acceptance/qualification authority surrounding the pinned SWAP5 scientific production baseline
guardrail: Acceptance authority is not an executable substitute and does not authorize unadmitted project-specific inputs.

evidence_statement: Live SWAP5 canonical head reviewed for this workunit is 80c6faaa8a277d9596a6da7bc5d2244c0df1bb82. Its F-CI91 closeout is governance-only RossFast preservation and records no scientific replay, production readmission or Status-A denominator change.
intended_use: Current governance/status context and proof that newest canonical head is not silently substituted for the pinned scientific production commit
guardrail: Do not use a moving current-canonical governance head as the reproducible scientific executable pin merely because it is newer.

evidence_statement: SWAP represents soil hydraulic behaviour per soil-physical layer using either analytical Mualem-Van Genuchten functions or hydraulic tables; analytical input includes residual/saturated water content, alpha, n, conductivity terms and saturated conductivity, while dry bulk density is also an explicit soil input.
intended_use: Define the target semantics of canonical hydraulic parameterization before SWAP serialization
guardrail: The SWAP input contract does not imply that bulk density uniquely determines the other hydraulic parameters.

evidence_statement: The Staringreeks provides Dutch class-based mean water-retention and hydraulic-conductivity characteristics for topsoil/subsoil classes and translation functions from basic soil characteristics.
intended_use: Modal hydraulic benchmark and profile-context prior
guardrail: Do not relabel a Staring/BOFEK modal characteristic as measured CURRENT anthropogenic compaction or as an observed uncompacted REFERENCE state.

evidence_statement: In the WUR/Flanders compaction study, pedotransfer functions estimated retention and conductivity from soil properties; adding bulk density as predictor reduced prediction error especially in the wet range, predicted curves were fitted with Mualem-Van Genuchten functions and used in SWAP experiments.
intended_use: Method precedent for a bulk-density-responsive H1 pedotransfer route
guardrail: The fitted functions and coefficients are study-domain methods/results and are not directly transferable Tollebeek parameters without domain review.

evidence_statement: Review evidence shows that accurate VGM pedotransfer estimates generally use multiple soil predictors such as texture, bulk density and organic matter; hydraulic prediction remains model/domain dependent and structural properties are important for further improvement.
intended_use: Support explicit multi-predictor/versioned PTF and uncertainty contract
guardrail: Bulk density alone is not sufficient evidence for a complete local hydraulic function.

evidence_statement: The BoVer experiments created multiple controlled compaction treatments with different dry bulk densities and used treatment-specific hydraulic properties in SWAP simulations.
intended_use: Support H0 direct-hydraulic-evidence route and treatment-specific state/hydraulic separation
guardrail: Experimental treatment parameters are method evidence, not Tollebeek state values or universal compaction multipliers.

evidence_statement: Field compaction experiments measured bulk density, penetration resistance, structural pore fractions and saturated hydraulic conductivity; compaction effects on water flow were associated with changes in structural pore space and conductivity.
intended_use: Support structural-connectivity guardrail for state-to-hydraulic transformation
guardrail: Equal or similar bulk density does not establish equal pore connectivity or hydraulic conductivity.

evidence_statement: Across four Dutch sandy-soil locations, silage-maize yield response depended on soil profile and weather. Average yield reductions reported for the experimental traffic treatments were about 15% at 10 Mg axle load and 4% at 5 Mg; reductions up to 38% occurred in some contexts.
evidence_value: 4-15 average treatment response; up to 38 context maximum
intended_use: Dutch maize response envelope and context evidence
guardrail: Axle-load treatment is not equivalent to current CC-NL severity or a national average damage coefficient.

evidence_statement: The study estimated that traffic-induced compaction associated with high axle loads reduced total Dutch silage-maize production by about 7% in its historical context.
intended_use: Historical Dutch sanity check only
guardrail: Do not use as a current national maize-loss coefficient or as a severity-class parameter.

evidence_statement: In the Oostwaardhoeve experiment on initially loosened sandy soil, grass dry-matter yield was highest at the moderate 4.5 t treatment; yield decreased with heavier treatment from that optimum, while the untrafficked 0 t treatment also yielded less than 4.5 t. The load effect was statistically significant.
intended_use: Guardrail and context evidence for grass response
guardrail: Do not infer a universal monotonic negative grass-yield response to increasing compaction or use treatment load as a national severity coefficient.

evidence_statement: On drought-sensitive sandy grassland at Cranendonck, compaction lowered yield in the first cut after establishment but later years showed significantly higher yields on loaded plots; improved moisture supply by capillary rise was identified as a plausible explanation.
intended_use: Guardrail and hydrological-context evidence for grass response
guardrail: Do not convert this experiment into a generic positive or negative grassland damage coefficient.

evidence_statement: For soil-improvement scenarios that remove moderate compaction, the report calculated 3-5% higher long-term average grassland yield.
intended_use: Long-term grass response proxy/scenario
guardrail: Inverse soil-improvement result; do not equate automatically with direct damage from a specified current compaction state.

evidence_statement: For very dry years, soil-improvement scenarios that remove moderate compaction produced 17-23% higher grassland yield because drought damage was reduced.
intended_use: Dry-year grass sensitivity scenario
guardrail: Do not use as annual expected damage without explicit dry-year frequency/context weighting.

evidence_statement: For soil-improvement scenarios, the report calculated up to 2% higher long-term average silage-maize yield.
intended_use: Long-term maize response proxy/scenario
guardrail: Inverse soil-improvement result; not a direct CC-NL severity coefficient.

evidence_statement: For dry-year soil-improvement scenarios, the report calculated 3-41% higher silage-maize yield, showing very strong profile and weather dependence.
intended_use: Dry-year maize sensitivity scenario
guardrail: Do not use as long-term average or current national damage coefficient.

evidence_statement: The published 2018 CC-NL dataset sampled more than one thousand locations across the Netherlands and provides the published national zero-measurement framework for agricultural-soil quality and its soil/land-use stratification.
intended_use: Structural reporting/domain basis and historical baseline
guardrail: Does not provide current 2026 compaction exposure and must not be treated as a current affected-area fraction.

evidence_statement: The repeat CC-NL project is publicly listed as active for 2024-2026. A bounded public-source review on 2026-09-18 did not identify a final published table that can supply current compaction exposure by land use × soil × depth × severity for this project.
intended_use: Current exposure acquisition/publication gate
guardrail: This is a dated public-route result and can become stale; it does not imply that no internal or forthcoming CC-NL exposure data exist.

evidence_statement: The definitive 2025 BRP crop-parcel dataset provides agricultural parcel geometry with the declared cultivated crop and is available through PDOK services/API. It can support a reproducible maize×soil spatial crosswalk.
intended_use: Current crop-area spatial crosswalk
guardrail: Crop geometry does not identify soil class or compaction exposure; overlay with a versioned compatible soil classification is required.

evidence_statement: CBS reports 183191 ha cultivated silage maize and 47.3 t/ha gross yield for 2025 (definitive), and 182587 ha cultivated silage maize for 2026 (provisional as of 2026-06-30).
intended_use: National closure/context for maize crop-area and yield work
guardrail: Do not distribute the national maize area proportionally over soil classes or use the national yield as a soil-specific compaction response.

evidence_statement: KWIN-AGV 2025 provides current crop-level gross money returns, allocated/direct costs and labour/cost information suitable for crop-specific accounting and damage calculations.
intended_use: Candidate crop-specific valuation input route
guardrail: Concrete KWIN values are not public in the current source set and are not admitted until accessed, recorded and linked to a valuation perspective.

evidence_statement: BINternet provides public current technical results, prices and balances from the Wageningen Social & Economic Research farm information network for represented farm/crop groups.
intended_use: Empirical valuation/context and plausibility route
guardrail: Do not substitute a farm-group balance for crop-specific marginal compaction damage without selecting and qualifying the exact variables and perspective.

evidence_statement: CC-NL 2018 reports six soil classes: sandy soils with an eerd layer at least 30 cm thick; other sandy soils; clay soils including clay-brick and old clay; loam soils including loam-brick; organic-mineral soils including organic podzols; and peat soils.
intended_use: Define the six-class reporting target for current crop×soil crosswalk work
guardrail: The six classes are reporting domains; this evidence alone does not provide a current polygon layer or current crop distribution.

evidence_statement: The 2018 land-use × soil-class area estimates were domain estimates based on LSK soil-profile descriptions from 1994-2001; the report explicitly notes that current classification may differ, especially for peat and organic-mineral soils.
intended_use: Guardrail for translating a current soil map into the historical six-class reporting system
guardrail: Do not describe a present-day BRO polygon overlay as a reconstruction of historical LSK domain membership.

evidence_statement: Official BRO SGM documentation exposes soil-unit code, soil classification, main soil classification and upper-profile soil characteristics in the downloadable soil model, providing a reproducible attribute basis for an explicit mapping to CC-NL6 classes.
intended_use: Candidate current spatial soil-classification route for BRP crop overlay
guardrail: The mapping from BRO attributes/codes to CC-NL6 is not automatic and must be reviewed code by code or by an explicitly documented rule.

evidence_statement: The BRO Bodemkaart is a national/regional soil model at approximately 1:50,000 scale and official guidance cautions that it is not, without additional information, a local parcel-scale soil survey.
intended_use: Set interpretation scale and uncertainty for crop×soil aggregation
guardrail: Do not interpret the soil class assigned to a BRP parcel intersection as a new field survey of that parcel.
